title: Semiconductor Supply Chain
question: How does a semiconductor go from an idea to a finished product?
description: An analysis of the companies, materials, manufacturing processes, information flows, and commercial relationships behind the semiconductor industry.

sections.title: Executive summary
sections.text: This project is in development. It explores how semiconductor companies, suppliers, and customers connect across the value chain. Findings and business implications will be published as the research develops.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Research scope: chip design, wafer fabrication, packaging and testing, electronics manufacturing, and the upstream suppliers supporting these activities.

sections.title: Methodology
sections.text: Planned approach: review primary company and industry sources, map the participants and handoffs, and distinguish physical product flows from information and commercial relationships.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.text: This section will explain each stage and the relationships between participants. Detailed explanations are pending research.

sections.title: Supply Chain Map
sections.text: The schematic below is an initial organizing framework, not a completed research finding. A semiconductor's actual path depends on its product and business model.

sections.title: Analysis
sections.text: Planned analysis: dependencies between stages, upstream inputs, information flows, and commercial relationships. Evidence and supporting diagrams will be added here.

sections.title: Key Findings
sections.text: Findings have not been published yet.

sections.title: Business Implications
sections.text: Implications will be drawn from the completed analysis.

title: Semiconductor Procurement & Supply Planning
question: How should a semiconductor manufacturer choose suppliers and protect production from shortages?
description: A practical sourcing and planning case study analyzing supplier cost, quality, lead time, capacity, delivery reliability, inventory, and risk.

sections.title: Executive summary
sections.text: This case study is in development. It will examine sourcing and supply planning decisions using clearly labeled data and assumptions. No supplier rankings or completed results are available yet.

sections.title: Business Problem
sections.text: How can supplier selection and order allocation support production requirements while accounting for cost, quality, delivery, and shortage risk?

sections.title: Background
sections.text: The scope will connect procurement decisions with demand, inventory, and production requirements.

sections.title: Methodology
sections.text: Planned approach: define demand requirements, document data sources and assumptions, compare suppliers, assess supply gaps, and evaluate allocation scenarios.

sections.title: Supplier Data
sections.text: Supplier data has not been added. Future tables will identify the source, units, reporting period, and whether values are observed or illustrative.

sections.title: Supplier Scorecard
sections.text: Planned criteria: cost, quality, lead time, capacity, and delivery reliability. Weights and scores will be documented before interpreting results.

sections.title: Demand Requirements
sections.text: Demand volumes and planning periods will be defined with their assumptions.

sections.title: Inventory
sections.text: Inventory balances and replenishment assumptions will be added here.

sections.title: Lead Times
sections.text: Supplier lead times and variability will be documented when data is available.

sections.title: Supply Gaps
sections.text: The analysis will compare available supply with demand by period.

sections.title: Safety Stock
sections.text: The calculation method and service-level assumptions will be explained before presenting any inventory recommendation.

sections.title: Supplier Capacity
sections.text: Capacity constraints and allocation assumptions will be documented here.

sections.title: Order Allocation
sections.text: Order allocation scenarios will be compared after supplier and demand data are defined.

sections.title: Risk Analysis
sections.text: Planned analysis: delivery variability, concentration risk, capacity constraints, and production exposure.

sections.title: Findings & Business Implications
sections.text: No findings have been published. Business implications will follow the analysis.

sections.title: Recommendation
sections.text: A recommendation will be added when supported by the data and documented tradeoffs.

sections.title: What I Learned
sections.text: Learning reflections will be added as the project progresses.
